analysis:
The change is confined to the test fixture in provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD/SSDOwnedEntryRetirementTests.swift (head lines 49-51, 62, 64). The fixture's SSDEvictableStore conformance now has `retireOwnedEntries(_:unusedSince:)`, and its private `retire` forwards an optional `unusedSince` cutoff to `SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove`. This is a protocol and signature adaptation, so the fixture mirrors a production-side API change. No production code is in this batch. Relevant threat: T-041 (SSD prefix-cache TTL/LRU at-rest retention, SEC-035). The change supports TTL retirement that spares entries hit after the cutoff, and the existing test at head lines 251-282 exercises it. Entries hit after their cutoff are kept, and the in-memory hit is recorded into the mtime without moving it backward. Without a cutoff, retirement stays unconditional, as tested at lines 278-281.

Nothing in the test code weakens a security control, and there is no new attack surface. Open integration question: the production implementation of `SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove(unusedSince:)` and the `SSDEvictableStore` callers (SSDBlockStore, SSDDiskBudget) are not in this batch. The next pass should confirm three points. First, that the TTL cutoff cannot be bypassed so that entries stay on disk beyond the 30-minute sliding TTL. Second, that rewriting the mtime to record a hit preserves no-follow and symlink safety (setAttributesIfSafe). Third, that the epoch-barrier ownership checks still run on every retirement path. The tests assert these behaviors but cannot establish them without the source.
